title: Barbershop Cost Per Lead in 2026: Real Numbers by Channel
summary: A barber shop click costs $0.94 to $1.09 on average in the US. See cost per lead at 5%, 10% and 15% conversion, channel benchmarks and a monthly budget.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- A click on the main barber shop searches costs $0.94 to $1.09 on average in the US, and $0.62 to $2.91 at the top of the page depending on the search.
- At an example click to lead rate of 10%, a $1.09 click works out to an $11 lead ($1.09 / 0.10 = $10.90). At 5% it is $22. Real campaigns often cost more, so measure your own.
- Meta is not cheaper here. LocaliQ's 2026 benchmarks for beauty and personal care show $39.25 per lead on Google search and $50.91 on Meta lead campaigns, about 30% more ($50.91 - $39.25 = $11.66).
- Starting budget formula: new clients wanted / booking rate x cost per lead. Start on one channel and adjust after a month of real data.


## What a click costs


These are the three searches most barber shop ads are built around. Prices are US figures for a click at the top of Google.


Keyword US searches a month Average click Top-of-page range


barber shop 823,000 $1.09 $0.67 to $2.91


barber near me 1,000,000 $0.94 $0.62 to $2.75


barbershop 823,000 $1.09 $0.67 to $2.91


The spread between the low and high end comes from three things. Competition matters most: in a dense city, several shops and booking apps bid on the same search, which pushes the price up. Location matters next, since the same search costs more in an expensive metro than in a small town. Urgency matters too. Someone typing "barber near me" often wants a cut today, and advertisers pay more to be in front of that person than for a general browser.


## From click to cost per lead


A click is not a lead. Your cost per lead is the click price divided by the share of clicks that turn into a call, booking or form. The table uses the main keyword, "barber shop", at its $1.09 average click. The conversion rates are examples, not benchmarks, and the last column assumes 1 in 3 leads books an appointment, also as an example.


Click to lead rate (example) Cost per lead Cost per booked appointment (1 in 3 books, example)


5% $22 ($1.09 / 0.05 = $21.80) $65 ($21.80 x 3 = $65.40)


10% $11 ($1.09 / 0.10 = $10.90) $33 ($10.90 x 3 = $32.70)


15% $7 ($1.09 / 0.15 = $7.27) $22 ($7.27 x 3 = $21.81)


Your conversion rate depends mostly on what happens after the click: the page, the offer and how fast you reply. For scale, a $39.25 lead at a $1.09 click implies about 36 clicks per lead ($39.25 / $1.09 = 36), or roughly 2.8%. That mixes a beauty industry benchmark with barber click prices, so treat it as an illustration only. To run your own numbers, use the[cost per lead calculator](https://www.sprites.ai/tools/cost-per-lead-calculator) .


## Google Ads vs Local Services Ads vs Facebook for barber shops


How you pay Intent When it wins for a barber shop


Google Ads search Per click, set by auction High. The person is searching for a barber now You want walk-ins and bookings from people nearby, and you can send them to a clear booking page


Local Services Ads Per lead, price set by Google by category and area High, where the category exists Only if Google offers a category that fits barbers in your area. It is built for service-call trades, and barber shops are generally not one of them, so check your account before planning around it


Facebook and Instagram (Meta) Per impression or click, with lead forms available Lower. People are scrolling, not searching You have an offer, such as a first-cut price or a membership, or want to bring back past clients and fill slow days


On Local Services Ads, Google charges per lead and sets the price by category and area, so there is no number worth quoting here. Our[guide to Google Local Services Ads](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/google-local-services-ads) explains how they work and which trades they suit.


Here are LocaliQ's 2026 benchmarks for cost per lead. The first pair is the figure for beauty and personal care, the closest industry to barber shops. The second is the all-industry average.


- **Beauty and personal care, Google search:** $39.25 per lead.
- **Beauty and personal care, Meta lead campaigns:** $50.91 per lead.
- **All industries, Google search:** $66.69 per lead.
- **All industries, Meta lead campaigns:** $27.39 per lead.


The order flips between the two sets. Across all industries Meta leads are cheaper than Google leads, but for beauty and personal care Google was cheaper. See our[cost per lead by industry](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/average-cost-per-lead-by-industry) page for more comparisons.


## How much to spend each month


Start from the clients you want, not from a round number.


**Monthly budget = (new clients wanted / booking rate) x cost per lead**


Worked example, with all inputs stated: you want 20 new clients a month, and say 1 in 3 leads books (a booking rate of one third). That needs 60 leads (20 x 3). At $21.80 a lead, the 5% example from above, the budget is $1,308 (60 x $21.80). At LocaliQ's 2026 beauty and personal care Google figure of $39.25, it is $2,355 (60 x $39.25). The gap between those two budgets is the reason to track your own cost per lead early.


Start on one channel, usually Google search, since people searching for a barber are close to booking. Give it a month of data, then add Meta only once you know your cost per lead and have an offer worth promoting. Running two channels on a small budget makes it hard to tell which one is working. For the wider plan, see our[barber shop advertising guide](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/barbershop-advertising) .


## How to lower your cost per lead


- **Lead with one clear offer.** A first-visit price or a set service price gives a new client a reason to book now. Vague ads such as "great haircuts" get fewer enquiries. To see what barber shops run on Facebook, browse the[barber shop ad examples](https://www.sprites.ai/barbershop-ads) .
- **Send clicks to a page built for booking.** Put the booking button, prices, hours and address at the top, and make sure it loads fast on a phone.
- **Answer fast.** A missed call or a slow reply to a message sends the client to the next shop. Use text back for missed calls and reply to enquiries within minutes.
- **Add negative keywords.** Exclude searches from people who are not clients, such as barber school, barber supply, barber jobs, barber license and clippers.
- **Limit the service area.** Target a radius around your shop, not a whole metro. People rarely travel far for a haircut, and distant clicks waste budget.
- **Keep lead form questions short.** Ask for name, phone, service and preferred time. Every extra field loses some people.
